newsitem.title: USA: At least two likely staged Olympics bombing - FBI.
newsitem.headline: At least two likely staged Olympics bombing - FBI.

text.p: Two or more people were probably responsible for last July's bombing in Atlanta's Olympic Park, FBI Deputy Director Weldon Kennedy said on Tuesday.

The July 27 blast during the Summer Olympic Games killed two people and injured over 100. Security guard Richard Jewell, who alerted authorities to a knapsack containing the bomb, was named as a suspect a few days after the bombing but was cleared on Oct. 26.
The FBI Monday released a tape recording of a telephone warning to Atlanta police 22 minutes before the bomb exploded. "There is a bomb in Centennial Park. You have 30 minutes," the caller said.

Asked on NBC-TV's "Today" programme if one person could have made the call and planted the bomb, Kennedy replied, "It's possible for one person to have done both. But it's more likely the work of two people or more."
The FBI is offering a $500,000 reward for any information that helps catch the bomber or bombers.
Kennedy said there were thousands of people in the park that night and it was possible someone had a photograph or a video tape of the person who planted the bomb.
At a news conference on Monday, Kennedy said the green military-style knapsack containing the 40-pound (18-kg) bomb was taken into the park an hour before the telephone call.
